newsitem.title: USA: Baxter to buy Research Medical for $236 million in stock.
newsitem.headline: Baxter to buy Research Medical for $236 million in stock.

text.p: Baxter International Inc., seeking to enhance its position as a major supplier of devices for heart surgery, said Wednesday it was acquiring Research Medical Inc. in a tax-free stock transaction valued at about $236 million.

Baxter, a global medical products company, said it entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Research Medical, a leading provider of specialised products used in open-heart surgery, for the equivalent of $23.50 a share.
Shares of Research Medical, which is based in Salt Lake City, jumped $2.875 to $22.875 in early trading on the Nasdaq market while Baxter fell 75 cents to $40.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Research Medical, which is also developing a line of products for use in minimally invasive cardiac surgery, reported $40 million in revenues for the fiscal year ended June 30, Baxter said.

"RMI's product line is a perfect complement to our own and represents a key step in reinforcing the leadership of Baxter's cardiovascular group in treating late-stage cardiovascular disease," Baxter group vice president Michael Mussallem said in a statement.
"The acquisition of RMI enables us to offer the most comprehensive line of products for open-heart surgery, encompassing implantable devices, disposables and services."
Baxter, based in Deerfield, Ill., said the deal is expected to close within 60 to 90 days and should add to its profits in 1998.
Baxter also said it will allocate a substantial portion of the purchase price to Research Medical's in-process research and development and treat it as an expense.
